title: Doug McIlroy's Garden-Hose Memo and the Invention of the Unix Pipe (1964-1973)
explainer: In an internal 1964 Bell Labs memo, Doug McIlroy proposed that programs should 'connect like a garden hose,' with the output of one screwed directly into the input of the next; Ken Thompson implemented the `|` pipe operator in Unix in 1973, instantly turning a set of small single-purpose tools into a combinable toolkit. That is exactly the move you make every time you pipe `grep` into `awk` into `sort` at an ops terminal, and the 'small composable tools joined by pipes' philosophy it kicked off still shapes how command-line and devops tooling is designed today.
